records.headline: FAA finalizes AD mandating replacement of A350 primary flight control actuators exposed to overload during acceptance testing
records.summary: The FAA published a final airworthiness directive (Federal Register doc 2026-11975) for all Airbus A350-941 and -1041 airplanes, prompted by a determination that certain primary flight control actuators (servo controls, electrical backup hydraulic actuators, electro-hydrostatic actuators) were exposed to mechanical overloads during acceptance test procedures, reducing fatigue life. The AD requires replacement of affected actuators and prohibits installation of affected parts; effective date reported as July 20, 2026.

references.ref_number: FAA-2026-3473 (Federal Register 2026-11975); claimed Project Identifier MCAI-2025-01221-T
references.effectivity: All Airbus SAS Model A350-941 and -1041 airplanes

records.root_cause: Mechanical overloads applied to certain primary flight control actuators during the manufacturing acceptance test procedure, reducing fatigue life of affected actuators.

records.headline: FAA AD on A330 standby fuel pump dormant failure trapping unusable fuel
records.summary: An FAA airworthiness directive effective June 8, 2026 applies to all Airbus A330-200, A330-200 Freighter, A330-300, and A330-841/-941 series airplanes. It was prompted by an in-service event and investigation finding that, under certain conditions, a dormant failure of a standby fuel pump could trap fuel in the aft section of the inner tank, rendering it unusable. The AD requires repetitive operational checks of standby fuel pumps, corrective action, and limits installation of affected parts.

records.root_cause: Dormant failure of a standby fuel pump can trap an amount of fuel in the aft section of the inner tank, rendering it unusable.

records.headline: GE90 HPT stage 1/2 disk iron-contamination AD (effective Feb 2026) — ongoing 777-300ER compliance burden
records.summary: FAA AD 2025-25-07 (published January 2, 2026, effective February 6, 2026) addresses iron-contamination in powder-metal HPT stage 1 and stage 2 disks on GE90-90B, -94B, -110B1, and -115B engines, which power 777-200ER/-200LR/-300ER/F aircraft. records.headline: Proposed FAA AD: cracked 777 MLG support beam lower stabilizer brace aft fitting — risk of gear collapse
records.summary: A proposed FAA AD covers Boeing 777-200, -200LR, -300, -300ER and 777F airplanes, prompted by reports of cracks on the main landing gear (MLG) support beam lower stabilizer brace aft fitting lower flange attachment holes. Uncorrected, the condition could lead to MLG collapse during takeoff/landing/ground operations, potential fuel tank breach, and fire/explosion risk. Comment period closed April 13, 2026; final-rule status as of the current window is unconfirmed.
records.root_cause: Cracking at MLG support beam lower stabilizer brace aft fitting lower flange attachment holes.

records.headline: UPS MD-11 (Flight 2976) crash investigation: NTSB hearing details Boeing pylon bearing fatigue failure history
records.summary: NTSB held a public hearing May 19-20, 2026 on the November 2025 fatal crash of UPS Airlines Flight 2976 (MD-11), reporting that fatigue cracking originated in a lubrication channel inside an engine-pylon aft-mount spherical bearing, and that Boeing's analysis of a 2002 in-service incident had masked the significance of nine subsequent occurrences before a 10th led to the fatal accident. UPS retired its 26-aircraft MD-11 fleet; FAA cleared the type to fly again in early May 2026 only with new spherical bearings and more frequent inspections. No probable cause has yet been determined; carried over as the 'UPS MD-11 class' major industry event of broad significance per project scope.
records.oem_regulator_position: FAA cleared MD-11 to resume flight in early May 2026 contingent on installation of new spherical bearings and increased inspection frequency; NTSB has not yet issued a probable cause finding.
records.root_cause: Fatigue cracking originating in a lubrication channel inside an aft-mount spherical bearing within the MD-11 engine pylon; reporting/analysis gaps at Boeing/FAA across at least 10 prior in-service bearing-failure occurrences (per NTSB hearing).
records.read_across: No MD-11s in CX fleet or peer list, but this is the flagship 'major industry event of broad significance' precedent (engine-pylon structural fatigue masked by incomplete incident-reporting/analysis) the digest is scoped to track per project convention; relevant as a regulatory-process precedent for how repeat minor failures can mask a systemic fatigue risk.
records.verifier_notes: Event (Nov 2025 crash) and hearing (May 19-20, 2026) are both outside the 7-day window; carried over per carry_developing_events:true because of the project's explicit 'UPS MD-11 class' significance threshold. Verifier should check NTSB.gov (ntsb.gov/investigations/Pages/DCA26MA024.aspx) for any update specifically dated within 2026-06-19–06-26 (e.g., docket releases, interim recommendations) before re-flagging as carryover vs new.

records.headline: Cathay Pacific A350-900 (CX156, Brisbane-Hong Kong) severe turbulence event injures 10; airline investigating
records.summary: Cathay Pacific flight CX156, an A350-900 (reg. B-LRV) flying Brisbane to Hong Kong, encountered severe turbulence about two hours from landing on May 23, 2026, during economy breakfast service. Ten people (4 passengers, 6 unbuckled crew) were injured, with 8 taken to hospital after landing; oxygen masks deployed and trolleys overturned. Cathay Pacific has opened an internal investigation into the weather forecast relayed to the crew and the response time; aviation-safety commentary notes high-altitude turbulence is difficult for radar to detect.
records.root_cause: Severe high-altitude turbulence encounter, reportedly difficult to detect via onboard weather radar; investigation into forecast accuracy and crew response ongoing.
records.verifier_notes: Event date 2026-05-23 is outside the 7-day lookback window (2026-06-19 to 2026-06-26); carried over as a directly fleet-relevant developing item (CX's own A350-900) pending any within-window update (e.g., HKCAD/AAIA preliminary finding, Cathay statement).
